The Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries, Rural Development, Water and Forests () is the ministry of the government of Morocco responsible for the preparation and implementation of state policy in the fields of agriculture, maritime fisheries, rural development, and the management of water and forests. It also intervenes in areas such as irrigation, the sanitary safety of agricultural and food production, agricultural training, and support for agricultural production sectors.
The ministry is headquartered in Rabat. Since October 2024, the Minister of Agriculture, Maritime Fisheries, Rural Development and Water and Forests has been Ahmed El Bouari. Maritime fisheries fall under a secretary of state attached to the ministry.
Responsibilities
The responsibilities of the ministry are defined by Decree No. 2.09.168, relating to the powers and organization of the central directorates of the Department of Agriculture. They include, in particular: Ministère de l'agriculture |url=https://www.agriculture.gov.ma/fr/ministere/missions |website=www.agriculture.gov.ma}}
* the preparation and implementation of government policy in the agricultural sector;
* the development of strategies related to agricultural production and the organization of production chains;
* the promotion of agricultural investment;
* the rational use of water resources for irrigation;
* the conduct of studies and research necessary for the development of agriculture at national and regional levels;
* the preparation of legislative and regulatory texts relating to agricultural activities;
* the collection, analysis, and dissemination of agricultural statistics and information;
* the preparation and implementation of state policy in the fields of higher agricultural education, agricultural research, and agricultural technical and vocational training;
* participation in negotiations and agreements relating to agricultural trade;
* monitoring national and international agricultural markets;
* the preparation of government policy regarding the sanitary safety of plants, animals, and food products;
* the definition and implementation of rural development policy, in coordination with the relevant government departments.
The ministry also serves as the secretariat of the permanent ministerial committee for the development of rural and mountainous areas.
National strategies
Plan Maroc Vert (2008–2020)
Launched in 2008 by former minister Aziz Akhannouch, the "Green Morocco Plan" (Plan Maroc Vert) sought to modernize the agricultural sector and promote higher-value agricultural exports. The strategy contributed to a significant increase in agricultural GDP, which rose from approximately MAD 65 billion to MAD 125 billion by 2020. However, the plan also raised concerns regarding the sustainability of water resources, particularly in arid regions.
Generation Green (2020–2030)
Succeeding the previous plan, the "Generation Green" strategy places greater emphasis on the human dimension of agricultural development. The program sets targets including the integration of 400,000 rural households into the middle class and the creation of 350,000 jobs for rural youth by 2030. It also promotes digital transformation in agriculture, climate resilience, and the adoption of more sustainable farming practices.
Specialized agencies and institutions
The ministry operates through a network of specialized public agencies and academic institutions:
* ONSSA: Responsible for food safety and animal health.
* Agricultural Development Agency (ADA): Handles technical investment and project implementation.
* National Agency for Water and Forests (ANEF).
* Morocco Foodex: Coordinates and controls agricultural and maritime exports.
* Academic Institutions: Includes the Hassan II Institute of Agronomy and Veterinary Medicine (IAV), the National School of Agriculture in Meknes (ENA), and the National Forestry School of Engineers (ENFI).
